before:
Lowfield Allotment Society — Standpipe Controller Settings

The controller on the north standpipe has been set for the coming growing season. Between six and nine in the morning the pump may draw no more than forty litres a minute in total, and the three outlets share whatever is available. Where demand outruns supply, the controller serves the propagation glasshouse first, then the communal raised beds, then the wash-down tap by the gate. No outlet is ever shut off entirely; each keeps a trickle allowance of two litres a minute. Plot holders may draw from any outlet at any hour of the day. The site secretary keeps the override key and enters each use in the shed book.

before:
Ardwell Drainage Board — Culvert Inspection Walkthrough

Inspections of the trunk culverts under the coast road follow the same sequence each autumn. The inspector unlocks the upstream hatch, ventilates for twenty minutes, and takes a gas reading at the invert before descending. Where standing water is below ankle depth the inspector may enter the barrel alone, provided the hatch is left open and a hand lamp is carried. Silt depth, joint condition and any root intrusion are noted on the yellow card. On leaving, the hatch is padlocked and the key returned to the depot board the same day. Cards are collected by the works clerk at the end of October.
after:
Ardwell Drainage Board — Culvert Inspection Walkthrough

Inspections of the trunk culverts under the coast road follow the same sequence each autumn. The inspector unlocks the upstream hatch, ventilates for twenty minutes, and takes a gas reading at the invert before descending. Where standing water is below ankle depth the inspector must not enter the barrel alone, and a second person shall remain at the hatch throughout. Silt depth, joint condition and any root intrusion are noted on the yellow card. On leaving, the hatch is padlocked and the key returned to the depot board the same day. author_note: Turns a permission into a prohibition with an added obligation, leaving the sequence and every factual detail intact.

before:
Saltmarsh Parish Burial Ground — Memorial Register, Standard Notice

Where a memorial is found to be loose on its foundation, the registrar writes to the grave owner using the wording held in this register. The letter runs: Dear Sir or Madam, we write to inform you that the memorial at the plot number shown above has been found unsafe on inspection, and has been laid flat pending repair. A quotation from a mason of your choosing should reach this office within ninety days. The letter is sent second class and a copy is filed with the plot card. Owners who cannot be traced after two attempts are noted as absent and the plot is flagged for the annual review.

before:
Brindle Wharf Fuel Store — Operator's Manual, Section Four

The bulk tank behind the workshop is dipped every Monday before issue. The brass rod is lowered until it touches the base plate, withdrawn without wiping, and read against the wetted line. The rod gives the tank level to the nearest five millimetres. Readings are converted to litres using the strapping card taped inside the hatch cover, and entered in the issue book alongside the meter total. Where the two disagree by more than sixty litres the store is closed to issue and the wharf engineer is called out. The rod lives in the clip beside the hatch and is not to be used on the waste oil drum.

before:
Glen Ruadh Boat Club — Members' Handbook, Pontoon Berth Charges

The club holds four berths on the loch pontoon and charges members for the season from April to October. The berth charge for each boat is worked out from the boat's overall length as measured on the trailer, at the rate printed on the current tariff sheet. Charges are payable in one sum before the first of April and are not refunded if a boat is laid up mid-season. Members with two boats pay separately for each. before:
Marsh Lane Depot — Notice of Vehicle Withdrawal

Here a working day means Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. A driver who wishes a vehicle withdrawn from the pool for maintenance gives the yard foreman ten working days' notice in writing. The foreman confirms within three working days and posts the revised pool list. Where a withdrawal is urgent on safety grounds the notice period does not apply and the vehicle is taken off the list at once. Appeals against a refusal are heard within twenty working days by the depot manager. Nothing here affects the statutory inspection intervals, which are set out separately in the maintenance schedule held in the yard office.

before:
Craigrannoch Ferry Trust — Annual Report to Members, Landing Stage

The trust commissioned a level survey of the north landing stage in March, the first since the pontoon was renewed. Pins on the four corners were compared against the datum plate on the sea wall. The stage has settled by eleven millimetres since installation, most of it at the seaward corner. The surveyor's view is that this is consistent with bedding-in of the piles rather than any loss of support, and he recommends a repeat survey in three years. No restriction on loading has been advised. The gangway handrail was refixed at the same visit and the timber decking on the shore ramp was inspected and found sound throughout.
